what: Re-mark ruled by Mide, 12 Nov 2026. The curling-stone answer (question what-forces-do-to-motion#explain) was already 2 marks out of 4: marks_available was 4 throughout, and 6 is the number of scheme points after the 11 Nov split (the 11 Nov report wrote this as '2/6', which was wrong). Mide's rule now pins it: marks available never change when points are split. The only change here is the note: one next step in plain words, no point numbers and no list of gaps (the new marker, run three times on the same answer, gave 2/4 with points 4 and 5 every time). Old values kept so the change can be undone. The child's own answer is deliberately not copied into this public repo.

old.feedback:
The idea that no force is needed to keep something moving, and that a force is only needed to change motion, are missing. Adding those ideas would make your explanation of why the stone keeps going much clearer.
Point 1: not yet — Says no force is needed to keep something moving.
Point 2: not yet — Says the forces on the stone are very nearly balanced, so the resultant is close to 0 N.
Point 3: not yet — Says a resultant force is only needed to change the motion.
Point 4: got it — Names friction with the ice, or air resistance, as a small backwards force.
Point 5: got it — Says that small backwards resultant force is what slows the stone.
Point 6: not yet — Says that on perfectly smooth ice it would not stop.
